security_audit.summary: The audit found confirmed setup risks from package-manager install commands and a hardcoded remote component URL. Most static hits are Markdown fences, TypeScript examples, documentation links, or placeholder environment setup. No prompt injection or hidden data-exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Pin package versions and provide reviewable source links before asking users to run npx or npm commands.
Use a versioned component URL or document an integrity check for the remote registry file.
Mark related-skill commands as optional and pin repository refs for reproducible installs.

content.value_statement: Teams need agent interfaces that handle streaming, tools, approvals, and widgets without rebuilding the runtime. This skill shows how to add agent-ui to React and Next.js projects with proxy-based inference.
actual_capabilities: Provides setup guidance for adding the Agent component to React or Next.js projects.
Shows a Next.js API proxy route using the Inference SDK.
Demonstrates runtime configuration for an assistant model and system prompt.
Describes streaming, widgets, approvals, and client-side tool lifecycle features.
Lists props for proxy URL, name, config, file uploads, and image uploads.
limitations: Depends on external inference.sh services and an API key.
Does not include a complete production backend or access-control policy.
Examples require React, Next.js, shadcn, and npm-compatible tooling.
Client-side tools need careful review before they modify user data.

use_cases.title: Embed a SaaS Copilot
use_cases.description: Add a chat agent to a product workflow with streaming responses and user approval states.

use_cases.title: Prototype an Assistant UI
use_cases.description: Test an agent interface in a React or Next.js application without building the runtime from scratch.

use_cases.title: Build Internal Tool Workflows
use_cases.description: Use widgets and approval flows to guide users through operational tasks and form updates.

prompt_templates.title: Add a Basic Agent
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-ui to add a simple assistant to my Next.js app. Include the install steps and proxy route placement.

prompt_templates.title: Configure Runtime Features
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure agent-ui with streaming, file upload settings, and a custom agent name for an internal support page.

prompt_templates.title: Add Client Tools
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a client-side tool plan for agent-ui that can inspect a form and propose field updates before applying them.

prompt_templates.title: Review Production Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my agent-ui integration for security, approval flows, environment variable handling, and user data boundaries before launch.

output_examples.input: Create an agent interface for a Next.js dashboard.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with install steps, proxy-route placement, component usage notes, and testing checks.

output_examples.input: Add human approval before the assistant changes a customer record.
output_examples.output: A flow design covering pending actions, approval states, result handling, and confirmation messages.

output_examples.input: Assess whether file uploads should be enabled.
output_examples.output: A risk summary covering allowed file types, privacy limits, preview behavior, and backend validation needs.

best_practices: Pin package versions and review remote component files before adding them to a project.
Keep API keys server-side and never expose them to browser components.
Require user approval before client-side tools submit forms or change records.
anti_patterns: Running remote install commands without checking the source and version.
Giving client-side tools unrestricted access to sensitive forms.
Treating example system prompts as complete production policies.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps you add a React or Next.js agent interface with streaming, tools, approvals, and widgets.

faq.question: Does it include backend logic?
faq.answer: It shows a proxy route using the Inference SDK, but production authorization remains your responsibility.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup example uses an Inference API key stored in a local environment file.

faq.question: Can the agent change forms?
faq.answer: The examples show client-side tools for form interaction. Review permissions before allowing changes.

faq.question: Is it safe to run the install commands?
faq.answer: Review the remote component source and pin versions before running package-manager commands.
